claims.text: The Pulumi `protect` resource option is a Pulumi-engine construct that is enforced entirely within the Pulumi engine.
The Pulumi `protect` resource option is never sent to the cloud provider.
Many cloud resources carry their own deletion-protection attributes that are separate from Pulumi's `protect` resource option.
A GCP Cloud SQL instance has a `deletionProtection` attribute (deletion-protection property).
An AWS RDS instance has a `deletionProtection` attribute (deletion-protection property).
Cloud resource deletion-protection attributes such as `deletionProtection` are enforced by the cloud provider independently of anything Pulumi knows about.

A resource can be unprotected in Pulumi (protect not set) and still refuse to delete because of the cloud provider's own deletion protection, or conversely be protected in Pulumi while the cloud provider's deletion protection is off.

The Pulumi docs page at /docs/iac/operations/troubleshooting/destroy-failures/ has a section 'Deletion protection on the resource itself' explaining how to tell Pulumi `protect` and cloud-provider deletion protection apart and resolve each.
In Pulumi, the `protect` resource option guards a resource within Pulumi (Pulumi refuses to delete it), independent of any protection enforced by the provider or cloud.
Many cloud resources carry their own deletion-protection attributes that are separate from Pulumi's `protect` option and are enforced independently by the provider or the cloud API.
A GCP Cloud SQL instance resource has a `deletionProtection` attribute (a deletion-protection setting enforced by the provider or cloud API, separate from Pulumi's `protect`).
An AWS RDS instance resource has a `deletionProtection` attribute (a deletion-protection setting enforced by the provider or cloud API, separate from Pulumi's `protect`).
Pulumi's `protect` option and a resource's own cloud-level deletion-protection attributes (e.g. `deletionProtection`) are complementary layers rather than substitutes for one another.
The page /docs/iac/operations/troubleshooting/destroy-failures/ has a section titled 'Deletion protection on the resource itself' (anchor #deletion-protection-on-the-resource-itself).

The 'Deletion protection on the resource itself' section of the destroy-failures troubleshooting page explains how to tell Pulumi's `protect` apart from resource-level deletion protection and how to resolve a destroy failure caused by either.

Protection against deletion of a resource can be held at three distinct layers (Pulumi's `protect` resource option, a provider-enforced flag, and a cloud-API-enforced protection), and the error message usually indicates which layer was hit during a `pulumi destroy` failure.
Pulumi's `protect` resource option is an engine-level guard that never reaches the cloud provider.
When a `pulumi destroy` fails because of the `protect` resource option, the error names a URN and mentions `protect`.
The page /docs/iac/concepts/resources/options/protect/ exists and explains how to remove the `protect` resource option.

Some Pulumi providers refuse to issue the delete call at all when a resource carries a deletion-protection attribute, and the failure surfaces from the provider before any request reaches the cloud API.
`gcp.sql.DatabaseInstance` has a `deletionProtection` attribute that is enforced by the Pulumi provider (refusing to delete before reaching the cloud API).
`gcp.container.Cluster` has a `deletionProtection` attribute that is enforced by the Pulumi provider (refusing to delete before reaching the cloud API).
Some clouds reject the delete call themselves, independent of Pulumi, and the error text comes back from the cloud provider's API, often with a distinct error code such as `ScopeLocked`.
AWS RDS `deletionProtection` is enforced by the cloud API and rejects delete calls independent of Pulumi.
AWS EC2 `disableApiTermination` is enforced by the cloud API and rejects delete calls independent of Pulumi.
An Azure Resource Manager management lock causes the delete call to be rejected by Azure independent of Pulumi, with an error code such as `ScopeLocked`.
`pulumi destroy` deletes what is already recorded in the stack's state, not what the Pulumi program currently says.

For provider-enforced and cloud-API-enforced deletion protection, setting the attribute to `false` in the Pulumi program is not enough on its own; the remediation is to set the attribute to `false`, run `pulumi up`, then run `pulumi destroy`.
Running `pulumi up` after setting the deletion-protection attribute to `false` propagates the change to both the live resource and Pulumi's state.

If deletion protection was already disabled outside of Pulumi (e.g., in the cloud console), `pulumi refresh` synchronizes the stack's state with reality, and `pulumi destroy` then succeeds without an intervening `pulumi up`.
`gcp.sql.DatabaseInstance` has a `deletionProtection` attribute that is provider-enforced.
`gcp.sql.DatabaseInstance` has a nested `settings.deletionProtectionEnabled` attribute that also guards the instance at the GCP API level.
`gcp.container.Cluster` has a `deletionProtection` attribute that is provider-enforced.
`gcp.bigquery.Table` has a `deletionProtection` attribute that is provider-enforced.
`gcp.bigquery.Dataset` has a `deleteContentsOnDestroy` attribute, and destroying a dataset that still contains tables fails unless it is `true`.
`aws.rds.Instance` and `aws.rds.Cluster` have a `deletionProtection` attribute that is enforced by the AWS API.
The `deletionProtection` attribute on `aws.rds.Instance` and `aws.rds.Cluster` defaults to `false`.
`aws.s3.BucketV2` has a `forceDestroy` attribute that defaults to `false`.
A non-empty S3 bucket (`aws.s3.BucketV2`) fails to delete unless `forceDestroy` is true.
`aws.ec2.Instance` has a `disableApiTermination` attribute that is enforced by the AWS API (EC2 termination protection).
`aws.dynamodb.Table` has a `deletionProtectionEnabled` attribute that is enforced by the AWS API.
The `deletionProtectionEnabled` attribute on `aws.dynamodb.Table` defaults to `false`.
`azure-native.authorization.ManagementLockByScope` and its scope-specific variants, e.g. `ManagementLockAtResourceLevel`, exist as resources for Azure management locks.

Any Azure resource under a management lock is protected by Azure Resource Manager, and a `CanNotDelete` lock must be removed before the resource can be deleted, independent of anything in the Pulumi program.
Destroying an `azure-native.keyvault.Vault` only soft-deletes it.
Recreating an Azure Key Vault with the same name as a soft-deleted vault fails with `VaultAlreadyExists` until the soft-deleted vault is purged or recovered.
Azure Key Vault purge protection prevents purging a soft-deleted vault until its retention period elapses.
